paper.title_en: Investigating fission fragments in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ir</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>193</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>→</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Bi</mi><none/><mo>*</mo><mprescripts/><none/><mn>205</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>lab</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>6.2</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>6.9</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>nucleon</mi></mrow></math>
paper.abstract_en: The production cross sections of 23 fission fragments in the mass range <math><mrow><mn>71</mn><mo>≤</mo></mrow><mo> </mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>141</mn></mrow></math> have been measured in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ir</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>193</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>lab</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>83.99</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mo>±</mo><mn>0.013</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mn>80.99</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.007</mn></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>74.82</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.026</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi></mrow></math> using the recoil-catcher activation technique followed by offline <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray spectroscopy. The mass and charge distributions of the fission fragments have been analyzed to study the isotopic and isobaric yield distributions. The mass dispersion parameter (<math><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></math>) for iodine isotopes is found to be <math><mrow><mn>4.66</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.82</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mn>4.04</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>3.13</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.39</mn></mrow></math> at <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>lab</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>83.99</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.013</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mn>80.99</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.007</mn></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>74.82</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.026</mn><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>MeV</mi></mrow></math>, respectively. The charge dispersion parameter (<math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msub></math>) for iodine isotopes is estimated to be 0.862, 0.799, and 0.709 at the respective energies. It has been observed that the fission fragment mass distribution displays well-described Gaussian functions, consistent with compound-nucleus fission. The variance of the fission-fragment mass distribution has been analyzed as a function of compound-nucleus temperature and found to increase exponentially with it. The variance is strongly influenced by entrance-channel mass asymmetry, highlighting the role of entrance-channel parameters. The present study also explores a linear dependence of mass variance on the deformation parameter (<math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>) of the target nuclei at the same excitation energy for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ir</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>193</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Tm</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>169</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> systems.
